# AgentPay

> AgentPay is an authorization and enforcement layer for agent purchases. It lets a user create a narrow payment mandate, approve it with a passkey, and revoke it immediately.

## Public entry points

- [Connect an MCP client](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/connect): user-facing instructions for connecting an authenticated agent.
- [Merchant demo](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/store): an example merchant checkout experience.
- [MCP endpoint](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/mcp): OAuth-protected Streamable HTTP MCP server.
- [MCP protected-resource metadata](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource): OAuth discovery for the MCP endpoint.
- [Merchant discovery example](https://agentpay-yuno.vercel.app/.well-known/agentpay.json): an example of a merchant-owned AgentPay manifest.

## Agent operating rules

- Authenticate to the MCP endpoint before using tools.
- Discover stores from their own product pages or `/.well-known/agentpay.json`; AgentPay is not a merchant directory.
- Start with `get_account`. If payment setup is required, use the browser link returned by `get_payment_setup_link` and never request card numbers, CVCs, PINs, bank passwords, or vault credentials in chat.
- Create the narrowest mandate that matches the user's request, then wait for the user to approve it with a passkey before purchasing.
- A purchase outside an active mandate must be escalated for a one-time approval. Do not retry a refused purchase without that approval.
- Revoke the mandate immediately when the user asks to stop.

## Indexing boundary

The sitemap intentionally contains only public HTML pages. APIs, OAuth flows, the MCP transport, authenticated screens, payment setup and registry endpoints are protocol surfaces rather than crawlable content; their supported methods and trust boundaries are listed in the route inventory.
